fix: centralize path safety and harden filesystem-touching tools (#7707)

## Summary

Centralizes file path-safety into a shared `agno.utils.path_safety`
module
and hardens 5 tool callers against path traversal, symlink escape,
control-char injection, Windows MagicDot, and Unicode normalization
attacks.

## Changes

- **NEW** `agno/utils/path_safety.py` with two helpers:
- `safe_join(directory, filename)` — filename-only validation (FileGen,
Slack)
- `safe_join_subpath(directory, subpath)` — multi-segment validation
with
containment via `resolve()` + `is_relative_to()` (Toolkit, is_safe_path,
FileTools)
  - Both NFKC-normalize input, reject control chars (Cc category) and
    Windows-reserved names, drive letters, UNC prefixes.
- **NEW** `agno.exceptions.PathSecurityError(AgnoError)` with
`status_code=400`.
- **DEPRECATED** `FileGenerationSecurityError` — kept as literal alias
of
`PathSecurityError` via PEP 562 module `__getattr__` (DeprecationWarning
on
  import). Will be removed in v2.7.
- Hardened: `FileGenerationTools._save_file_to_disk`,
`SlackTools._save_file_to_disk`,
`Toolkit._check_path`, `agno.skills.utils.is_safe_path`,
`FileTools.check_escape`.
- Refactored 4 `generate_*_file` methods to share post-write logic.
- Bumped `requires-python = ">=3.9,<4"` (required for
`Path.is_relative_to`).

## Review feedback addressed (latest 4 commits)

Follow-up commits in response to reviewer comments on this PR:

- **`fix(path_safety): harden cross-platform Windows validation`**
[C1+C2]
- `safe_join` validates raw input via `PureWindowsPath` BEFORE
`Path.name`
strips the drive on Windows (closes the bypass where
`Path("C:\\evil.txt").name == "evil.txt"`).
- `safe_join_subpath` applies per-segment validation (control chars,
drive/UNC,
Windows reserved names, MagicDot rstrip) on every segment after
splitting
    on both `/` and `\\`.
  - Shared `_validate_segment` helper keeps both helpers in sync.

- **`fix(slack): align error contract + harden download_file`**
[H1+H3+H4]
- `_save_file_to_disk` raises `PathSecurityError` instead of swallowing
    (sister-method alignment with `FileGenerationTools`).
  - `upload_file` catches `PathSecurityError` and surfaces additive
    `local_path_error` field — Slack delivery still proceeds.
- `download_file` routes both branches through `safe_join_subpath`
(`dest_path`
multi-segment) and `safe_join` (`filename` basename); requires
`output_directory`
when `dest_path` is supplied; preserves OSError → `content_base64`
fallback.

- **`fix(file_generation, path_safety): observable filename
sanitization`** [H2+H5]
- `safe_join` emits `log_warning` when discarding path components,
pointing
    to `safe_join_subpath` as the alternative; docstring gets explicit
    `.. warning::` block.
- `_save_file_to_disk` returns `Tuple[Optional[str], str]` (saved path +
the
sanitized basename); `_finalize_generation` uses the sanitized basename
    for `File.filename` so it always matches `Path(File.filepath).name`
    (single source of truth at the artifact layer; CWE-179).

- **`test(file_generation): rename
test_url_encoded_traversal_rejected`** [C3]
- Renamed to
`test_url_encoded_traversal_sanitized_inside_output_directory` —
`%2e%2e` is not URL-decoded; the test asserts containment, not
rejection.

## Tests

- 26 unit tests for `path_safety` module + **10 new** for raw-input
drive/UNC
  rejection, per-segment validation, and `log_warning` observability.
- 27 cross-tool consistency + 9 adversarial attack tests + **1 new**
parametrized
  `test_subpath_callers_reject_reserved_segment` (4 cases).
- 19 `FileGenerationTools` tests + **3 new** for `File.filename`
round-trip.
- 5 `SlackTools` security tests (1 renamed + **1 new** for OSError
fallback)
+ **4 new** in `test_slack_tools.py` for `local_path_error` and
`download_file`
  `dest_path` happy/sad paths.
- 5 `Toolkit._check_path` tests covering multi-segment + symlinked-base
bypass.

**~110 new/changed tests. All passing on Python 3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12.**
Verified end-to-end with a real OpenAI agent and FastAPI HTTP backend.

## Backward compatibility

`FileGenerationSecurityError` continues to work via the literal alias —
it
refers to the **same class object** as `PathSecurityError`, so code that
catches either name keeps working bidirectionally:

```python
from agno.exceptions import FileGenerationSecurityError  # DeprecationWarning
try:
    ...
except FileGenerationSecurityError:  # Still catches PathSecurityError raises
    ...
```

Migrate when convenient:

```python
from agno.exceptions import PathSecurityError
try:
    ...
except PathSecurityError:
    ...
```

## Behavior changes (downstream-visible)

From the original PR:
- `_check_path` and `is_safe_path` now reject control characters,
Windows-reserved
names (CON, PRN, etc.), drive letters (`C:\`), UNC paths
(`\\server\share`),
and Unicode-normalized traversal. Previous behavior silently accepted
these.
- `_check_path` now resolves both `base_dir` AND `file_path` before
containment
  check (fixes pre-existing symlinked-base-dir bypass).

Added by the follow-up commits:
- `safe_join_subpath` rejects path SEGMENTS named
`CON/AUX/NUL/PRN/COM[1-9]/LPT[1-9]`
on every OS (defense-in-depth). A POSIX user with a literal folder named
`aux/` would now be rejected — accepted tradeoff for cross-platform
consistency.
- `SlackTools._save_file_to_disk` now **raises `PathSecurityError`** on
filename rejection instead of returning `None`. Public methods
(`upload_file`,
  `download_file`) catch and surface a structured error to the agent.
- `SlackTools.upload_file` adds a new additive `local_path_error` field
to the
JSON response when local persistence is rejected; Slack delivery itself
still
succeeds. Existing `local_path` field is unchanged on the success path.
- `SlackTools.download_file` requires `output_directory` whenever
`dest_path` is
  supplied (closes the previous write-anywhere case). Returns
`{"error": "Invalid destination path: ..."}` on rejection instead of
falling
  back to base64 (the LLM agent now sees the rejection explicitly).
- `FileGenerationTools` `File.filename` is now the **sanitized
basename**
(matching `File.filepath`). Callers reading back the original
LLM-supplied
name will see a sanitized value when input contained path components or
trailing dots/spaces. **This is wire-visible via AgentOS JSON
serialization.**
- `safe_join` emits `agno.utils.log.log_warning` when path components
are
  stripped (observability — no behavior change beyond the log line).

fix: add aiohttp to slack extra dependencies (#7939)

## Summary
- Adds `aiohttp>=3.7.3,<4` to the `slack` optional extra in
pyproject.toml

## Problem
`AsyncWebClient` from `slack_sdk` imports `aiohttp` at **module load
time**, not lazily. This means:
1. User runs `pip install agno[slack]`
2. User tries to use Slack interface
3. `ImportError: No module named 'aiohttp'`

This affects ALL Slack operations (streaming and non-streaming) because
the import happens unconditionally.

## Why this version constraint
- `>=3.7.3` — when aiohttp stabilized the async context manager API used
by AsyncWebClient
- `<4` — matches slack_sdk's own constraint for aiohttp

fix: use stream_events instead of stream_steps for AG-UI teams (#7938)

## Summary

Fixes a typo introduced in #5092 (Oct 2025) that caused teams running
via AG-UI to miss all intermediate streaming events.

- When `stream_intermediate_steps` was renamed to `stream_events` in
#5092, the agent path was correctly updated but the team path was
mistyped as `stream_steps`
- Since `Team.arun()` accepts `**kwargs`, the invalid parameter was
silently swallowed
- Teams via AG-UI have been missing intermediate events (tool calls,
reasoning steps, member delegations) for ~7 months

## The Bug

```python
# Agent path (line 57) - CORRECT
stream_events=True

# Team path (line 99) - WRONG (was stream_steps=True)
stream_events=True  # Fixed
```

## Impact

When `stream_events` is not set (defaults to `False`):
- No run lifecycle events (`TeamRunStartedEvent`,
`TeamRunCompletedEvent`)
- No intermediate step events (reasoning, tool calls, member delegation)
- Only final content is streamed to AG-UI frontend

## Related Issues

- #5453 - Team streaming issues with `respond_directly=True`
(potentially related symptom)
- #5092 - Original PR where the typo was introduced

feat: add Gemini managed agents (Deep Research + Antigravity) to GeminiInteractions (#7975)

## Summary

Adds first-class support for Google's managed agents on the Gemini
Interactions API:

- **Deep Research** (`deep-research-preview-04-2026`,
`deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025`) — autonomous research agent that
runs in the background and returns a researched report with citations.
- **Antigravity** (`antigravity-preview-05-2026`) — general-purpose
autonomous agent (Gemini 3.5 Flash) that plans, runs code, browses, and
produces artifacts inside a managed Linux sandbox.

Both share a single agent path (`agent` + `agent_config` instead of
`model` + `generation_config`); per-agent semantics are encoded in the
model.

### Model class (`GeminiInteractions`)

- **Agent path**: new `agent` field switches the request to `agent` +
`agent_config`. The SDK enforces these are mutually exclusive with
`model` + `generation_config`.
- **Per-agent forcing**:
- Deep Research → `background=True` + `store=True` (required by the
API).
- Antigravity → `store=True` only; `background=True` is rejected by the
SDK.
- **Deep Research config knobs**: `collaborative_planning`,
`thinking_summaries`, `visualization` (emitted as `agent_config` only
for `deep-research*` agents).
- **Antigravity environment**: new `environment` field accepts
`"remote"`, `"env_<id>"` (reuse), or a full `EnvironmentConfig` dict.
Forwarded on the agent path; silently dropped on the model path.
- **Tools**: `mcp_servers` (remote MCP) and `file_search_store_names`
(File Search) supported on the agent path where the agent allows them.

### Background streaming (Deep Research)

Background SSE streams end early and continue server-side.
`invoke_stream` / `ainvoke_stream` now track `interaction_id` +
`last_event_id` and reconnect via `interactions.get(id, stream=True,
last_event_id=...)` until terminal, mirroring the API's reference flow
(and surviving the documented ~600s connection drop). Antigravity does
not run in background, so the reconnect loop is gated off for it.

### Stream events

- `InteractionStatusUpdate` (progress).
- `ErrorEvent` (raises `ModelProviderError`).
- `DeltaImage` (streamed visualization charts).
- A `failed` interaction status now raises `ModelProviderError` with the
API's error detail instead of returning an empty response.

### Server-side history

When `previous_interaction_id` is set, only the new turn is sent (the
API holds prior history). On the agent path the framework's
auto-injected system prompt is dropped — Deep Research and Antigravity
reject `system_instruction` and treat `input` as the request.

### Cookbooks

Under `cookbook/90_models/google/gemini_interactions/`:

- `deep_research.py`, `deep_research_streaming.py`,
`deep_research_collaborative_planning.py`,
`deep_research_file_search.py`, `deep_research_mcp.py`,
`deep_research_multimodal.py`, `deep_research_visualization.py`
- `antigravity.py`, `antigravity_streaming.py`,
`antigravity_environment_config.py`

### Tests

`TestDeepResearchAgentPath`, `TestAntigravityAgentPath`,
`TestAgentBackgroundPolling`, `TestBackgroundStreamReconnect`,
`TestParseInteractionResponse` (citations + failed-status). 110 unit
tests pass.

The model path (`GeminiInteractions(id="...")`) is unchanged; a
regression test enforces the non-background path never enters the
reconnect loop.

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **Antigravity:** Added first-party support for Google's Antigravity
API in two shapes — `AntigravityAgent` (a `BaseExternalAgent` served
through AgentOS with native sessions/streaming/UI) and
`AntigravityTools` (a `Toolkit` that lets any Agno agent delegate a
sub-task to a managed Antigravity sandbox).
- **Gemini Managed Agents:** Added `GeminiInteractions` support for
Google's managed agents — **Deep Research** (autonomous research with
citations, background streaming with reconnect/`last_event_id` resume)
and **Antigravity** (general-purpose agent in a managed Linux sandbox).
New `agent` / `agent_config` / `environment` fields, per-agent forcing
of `background` and `store`, and support for `mcp_servers` +
`file_search_store_names` on the agent path.
- **Cookbook - Data Labeling:** Added `cookbook/data_labeling/` with 18
self-contained workflows covering text, image, audio, video, document,
and composed (LLM-as-judge, quality review) labeling primitives.
- **Cookbook - Slack HITL:** Added a deterministic Slack HITL
incident-commander demo showing structured pauses via
`tool_choice="required"`, user_input echo, and clean termination via
`stop_after_tool_call=True`.

## Improvements:

- **Path Safety (Security):** Centralized path-safety into a new
`agno.utils.path_safety` module with `safe_join` and
`safe_join_subpath`. Hardened `FileGenerationTools`, `SlackTools`,
`Toolkit._check_path`, `agno.skills.utils.is_safe_path`, and
`FileTools.check_escape` against path traversal, symlink escape,
control-char injection, Windows MagicDot, and Unicode normalization
attacks. Introduced `PathSecurityError` (`FileGenerationSecurityError`
kept as deprecation alias). Bumped `requires-python` to `>=3.9,<4`.
- **Parallel MCP:** `ParallelMCPBackend` now sends `User-Agent:
agno/<version>` on every request so Parallel can attribute traffic to
agno.
- **Evals Config:** Dropped the unused `available_models` field from
`EvalsDomainConfig`; the top-level `AgentOSConfig.available_models` is
now the only supported source for the Evals UI dropdown.
- **Chonkie:** Updated chonkie dependency pin (follow-up to #7869).
- **Cookbook:** Renamed `gemini-3-flash-preview` to `gemini-3.5-flash`
across the Gemini Interactions cookbooks.

## Bug Fixes:

- **AG-UI Teams:** Fixed a typo (`stream_steps` → `stream_events`) that
caused teams running via AG-UI to silently drop all intermediate
streaming events (lifecycle, reasoning, tool calls, member delegations)
for ~7 months.
- **Slack Extra:** Added `aiohttp>=3.7.3,<4` to the `slack` optional
extra — `AsyncWebClient` imports `aiohttp` at module load, so `pip
install agno[slack]` was broken for all Slack operations.
- **Google Drive:** Surfaced the Drive API `incompleteSearch` flag from
`GoogleDriveTools.search_files()` so `corpora="allDrives"` callers can
detect when Drive did not search every drive.
- **GeminiInteractions:** Added a `generation_config` passthrough field
for advanced controls (`top_k`, `presence_penalty`, etc.) and fixed
history handling — when `previous_interaction_id` is set, only the new
turn is sent rather than replaying the full history. Now actually
leverages server-side statefulness.
- **Anthropic Server Tools:** Preserved `server_tool_use` and
code-execution content blocks in message history so multi-turn
server-tool flows no longer break across turns.
- **Anthropic Hardening:** Follow-up to the above — switched to the
canonical `redacted_thinking` type literal (the SDK rejects
`redacted_reasoning_content`), accepted both spellings on the streaming
start event, added a dedup guard on round-tripped server tool blocks,
made coercion failures visible via `log_warning`, and coerced non-block
tool-result items to text.
- **Gemini Errors:** Generic Gemini errors now include the exception
type when `str(error)` is empty or weak, preserving error context across
`invoke` / `invoke_stream` / `ainvoke` / `ainvoke_stream`.
- **N1N:** Added the missing `n1n` provider mapping in `get_model()` so
`Agent(model="n1n:...")` model-string paths now resolve correctly.

Replace all `datetime.utcnow()` calls with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`
in `libs/agno/agno/learn/stores/decision_log.py`.

## Problem

`datetime.utcnow()` has been [deprecated since Python
3.12](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime.utcnow)
because it returns a naive `datetime` that doesn't carry timezone
information, making it ambiguous.

- Updated `from datetime import datetime` to `from datetime import
datetime, timezone`
- Replaced 4 occurrences of `datetime.utcnow()` with
`datetime.now(timezone.utc)`:

- `_extract_decisions_from_messages()` - setting `created_at` for new
decisions
  - `_aextract_decisions_from_messages()` - async version of the above

## Before/After

**Before (deprecated):**
```python
decision.updated_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
```  

**After (recommended):**
```python
decision.updated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
```  

## Verification

- This is a mechanical replacement with no behavioral change
- `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` returns the same UTC instant but as a
timezone-aware object
- The `.isoformat()` output gains a `+00:00` suffix, which is valid ISO

fix(pgvector): make prefix_match=True actually do prefix matching (#8048)

## Summary

`PgVector(prefix_match=True)` is currently a silent no-op. The flag is
advertised in the constructor docstring as *"Enable prefix matching for
full-text search"* — the implementation appends `*` to each query word,
then feeds the result to `websearch_to_tsquery`, which doesn't honour
`*` as a wildcard. The `*` is silently dropped or escaped before the
tsquery is built, so `prefix_match=True` produces identical SQL to
`prefix_match=False`. Partial queries like `"ani"` never FTS-match
documents containing `"animal"` even though that's the whole point of
the flag.

This PR routes through `to_tsquery` when prefix matching is on. Postgres
`to_tsquery('english', 'ani:*')` does prefix-aware lexeme matching: the
lemma `anim` (which `animal` lemmatizes into) is matched by the `ani:*`
prefix.

## Implementation

New private helper `_build_ts_query(query)` returns the right function
expression based on `self.prefix_match`:

- **off:** `websearch_to_tsquery(language, query)` — unchanged from
today
- **on:** `to_tsquery(language, "tok1:* & tok2:* & …")` after tokenizing

in user input are stripped during tokenization — they'd otherwise make

callers can short-circuit.

public surface for backwards compatibility, with an updated docstring
pointing at `_build_ts_query` as the correct path.

search with default weights):

| `wildlif` | top 5 @ 0.50+ | same |

unchanged because their full lexemes already match via the default path.

fix: use is not None for temperature/top_p/top_k across all Claude variants (#8009)

## Summary

Fixes #8004

`get_request_params` in all three Claude variants (Anthropic, AWS,
VertexAI) used bare truthiness checks when deciding whether to include
float sampling parameters. Because `0.0` is falsy in Python, any of
these set explicitly to `0.0` / `0` were silently dropped and the API
fell back to its own defaults (temperature ~1.0). This broke every use
case relying on `temperature=0` for deterministic output, with no
warning or error.

## Root cause

```python
# BEFORE (buggy) — same pattern in anthropic/claude.py, aws/claude.py, vertexai/claude.py
if self.temperature:          # 0.0 is falsy → silently dropped
    _request_params["temperature"] = self.temperature
if self.top_p:                # same bug
    _request_params["top_p"] = self.top_p
if self.top_k:                # same bug
    _request_params["top_k"] = self.top_k
```

## Fix

```python
# AFTER — only skip when the caller never set the param
if self.temperature is not None:
    _request_params["temperature"] = self.temperature
if self.top_p is not None:
    _request_params["top_p"] = self.top_p
if self.top_k is not None:
    _request_params["top_k"] = self.top_k
```

`stop_sequences` keeps its truthiness guard (an empty list `[]` should
not be sent).

- `agno/models/anthropic/claude.py` — original fix
- `agno/models/aws/claude.py` — same fix applied (identical bug)
- `agno/models/vertexai/claude.py` — same fix applied (identical bug)
- `tests/unit/models/test_claude_request_params.py` — 17 new tests
covering zero values, None exclusion, and positive values across all

with no usable tokens (empty/symbol-only input) previously built

(upstream `prefix_match` fix in PgVector).

Now that `prefix_match=True` actually routes through
`to_tsquery('tok:*')` instead of getting silently stripped by
`websearch_to_tsquery`, the image_search cookbook flips it on. The
demo's headline UX win: typing a partial word like `ani` or `mount`
returns primary results (animals, mountains) instead of falling under
the "no exact match — showing closest" tray.

**Query-battery delta** (12 queries, 38-image Picsum index,
`SCORE_FLOOR=0.30`):

| Query   | Primary tier before | Primary tier after |
|---------|---------------------|--------------------|
| `ani`   | 0                   | **6**              |
| `mount` | 1                   | **8**              |
| `car` | 0 | 1 (leopard via "carnivore" prefix collision) |
| others  | unchanged           | unchanged          |

`anima` is an instructive non-win: the document side stores the
stemmed lexeme `anim`, and `to_tsquery('anima:*')` requires lexemes
that *start with* `anima` — the stem doesn't qualify. This is
inherent to FTS stemming. The tray fallback catches it.

The `SCORE_FLOOR=0.30 + tail-tray` logic in `public/index.html` stays
useful for genuine no-FTS queries (`night city`, `asdf`), just
triggers less often. The accompanying inline comment was refreshed
since "car" is no longer the canonical no-FTS example.

Full before/after numbers are in

[`cookbook/data_labeling/image_search/TEST_LOG.md`](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/ab/image-search-prefix-match/cookbook/data_labeling/image_search/TEST_LOG.md).

refactor: simplify Calendar and Gmail context provider instructions (#7982)

## Summary

Removes duplicated documentation from context provider instructions.
Providers now contain only what's **unique to the provider layer**.

**Before:** 157 lines duplicating toolkit content (tool lists, parameter
docs, query syntax)
**After:** 27 lines of role + behavior + safety

## Two-Layer Instruction Architecture

When a context provider sub-agent runs, it receives instructions from
TWO sources:

| Layer | Source | What It Should Contain |
|-------|--------|------------------------|
| **Toolkit** | `CALENDAR_INSTRUCTIONS`, `GMAIL_QUERY_INSTRUCTIONS` (via
`add_instructions=True`) | Technical reference: date formats, query
syntax, tool tips |
| **Provider** | `DEFAULT_READ_INSTRUCTIONS`,
`DEFAULT_WRITE_INSTRUCTIONS` | Behavioral: role, safety rules,
confirmation policies, scope |

### Before (duplicated)

Provider instructions repeated content already in the toolkit:
- Tool parameter lists (`time_min`, `time_max`, etc.)
- Gmail query syntax (`from:`, `is:unread`, `newer_than:`)
- Calendar date formats (ISO 8601)

### After (clean separation)

**Provider owns (unique):**
- Role definition ("You answer questions by searching...")
- Behavioral guidance (ask timezone, cite results, verify recipients)
- Safety rules (confirm ambiguous, confirm delete, draft by default)
- Scope boundaries ("Read-only")

**Toolkit owns (technical reference):**
- `CALENDAR_INSTRUCTIONS`: Date/time formats, tool tips
- `GMAIL_QUERY_INSTRUCTIONS`: Query syntax
- `GMAIL_COMPOSE_INSTRUCTIONS`: Compose patterns

## Summary

On the agent path (Antigravity, Deep Research), `FunctionCallStep`s in
the Interactions API response describe tools that the autonomous loop
executes inside the server-managed sandbox (e.g. Antigravity's
`list_files`, `read_file`, browser ops). The current code surfaces them

chore: Release v2.6.9 (#8042)

# Changelog

## New Features:

- **Approvals - Resolved Approval in Post-Hooks:** Post-hooks and
observability integrations can now read the full resolved approval
record (`resolved_by`, `resolved_at`, etc.) via
`run_response.metadata["approval"]`. Previously only `status` and
`resolution_data` were exposed. Lives in `metadata` so it works
uniformly across `RunOutput` / `TeamRunOutput` / future
`WorkflowRunOutput`. (#7366, #8032)

## Improvements:

- **PgVector - prefix_match=True actually works:**
`PgVector(prefix_match=True)` was a silent no-op - it appended `*` then
routed through `websearch_to_tsquery`, which ignores wildcards. Now
routes through `to_tsquery('tok:*')` with proper tokenization, so
partial queries like `"ani"` FTS-match `"animal"` as documented. New
cookbook `cookbook/07_knowledge/04_advanced/06_prefix_search.py` shows
the help-center typeahead use case. (#8048, #8051, #8052)
- **PgVector - empty-tsquery fallback robustness:** Replaced the
`to_tsquery(language, '')` fallback with a literal `''::tsquery` cast so
behavior no longer depends on the parser tolerating empty input. (#8053)
- **Claude variants - temperature/top_p/top_k = 0 honored:** Anthropic,
AWS, and VertexAI Claude variants were silently dropping `0.0` values
due to bare truthiness checks. Switched to `is not None` so
deterministic output works as intended. (#8009, fixes #8004)
- **Calendar & Gmail context providers - clean instruction layering:**
Trimmed `DEFAULT_READ_INSTRUCTIONS` / `DEFAULT_WRITE_INSTRUCTIONS` from
157 lines to 27 by removing content already supplied by the toolkit-side
instructions. Provider now owns role + safety; toolkit owns the
technical reference. (#7982)
- **decision_log - drop deprecated `datetime.utcnow()`:** Replaced with
`datetime.now(timezone.utc)` to clear the Python 3.12 deprecation
warning. (Closes #8030)
- **Chonkie:** Bumped to `>=1.6.7` to pick up the upstream language
auto-detection fix; removed the temporary test workarounds from #7904.
(#8012)

## Bug Fixes:

- **GeminiInteractions - server-side tool calls leaking onto the agent
path:** On the agent path (Antigravity, Deep Research),
`FunctionCallStep`s describe tools the autonomous loop runs inside the
server-managed sandbox. Previously we surfaced them as local
`tool_calls`, leading to `Function <name> not found` and follow-up `400
invalid_request` errors. Gated the `FunctionCallStep` branch on
`self.agent is None` for both streaming and non-streaming. Model path
with user-declared tools is unchanged. (#8045)
- **Claude (Anthropic / AWS / VertexAI) - `temperature=0` silently
dropped:** See Improvements. Every prior release silently fell back to
API defaults (~1.0) when callers explicitly set `0`. (#8009, fixes
#8004)

fix: truncate HITL card body to prevent silent Slack rejection (#8072)

## Summary

Slack Block Kit rejects **Card block** body text longer than 200
characters with `invalid_blocks` error, causing HITL approval cards to
silently fail to render. When this happens, agents pause indefinitely
waiting for approval that can never come.

This fix truncates the card body text using the existing `truncate()`
helper (already in `types.py`) before building the card.

## Changes

- Import `truncate` from `agno.os.interfaces.slack.types`
- Apply `truncate(body_text, 200)` in `_build_confirmation_card()` 
- Apply `truncate(body_text, 200)` in `build_confirmation_toggle_card()`
- Add 2 tests verifying truncation behavior

## Root cause

Tool calls like `comment_on_issue` with 250+ character arguments cause
the body text to exceed [Slack's Card block body limit of 200
chars](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/card-block/).
The card post request returns `ok: false` with `invalid_blocks` error,
but this was not being detected — the agent just hangs waiting for
approval.

Note: Section blocks have a 3000 char limit, but agno's HITL cards use
the newer Card block type (2024) which has stricter limits.

## How it was discovered

agno-agi/coda#23 implemented a monkey-patch workaround
(`coda/slack_patches.py`) to fix this. This PR moves the fix upstream
where it belongs.

(`application/octet-stream`), so the routers' `content_type`-only check
rejected them even though `text/markdown` was whitelisted.
- Anthropic's text document source only accepts `media_type:
"text/plain"`, but we were forwarding the real subtype (text/markdown,
text/csv, ...), causing a 400.

## Summary

in `YouTubeReader.async_read()`

fix: replace deprecated asyncio.get_event_loop() with get_running_loop() in embedders (#8111)

## Summary

Replace `asyncio.get_event_loop()` with `asyncio.get_running_loop()` in
three embedder modules (6 occurrences total).

## Motivation

`asyncio.get_event_loop()` was deprecated in Python 3.10
([docs](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-eventloop.html#asyncio.get_event_loop)).
When called inside an `async def` method — which is the case for all six
call sites — `asyncio.get_running_loop()` is the correct modern API. It:

1. Avoids the `DeprecationWarning` emitted in Python 3.10+
2. Is semantically precise — these methods can only be called from a
running loop
3. Fails fast with `RuntimeError` if accidentally called outside an
async context, rather than silently creating a new loop

## Changes

| File | Occurrences |
|------|-------------|
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/embedder/fastembed.py` | 2
(`async_get_embedding`, `async_get_embedding_and_usage`) |
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/embedder/sentence_transformer.py` | 2
(`async_get_embedding`, `async_get_embedding_and_usage`) |
| `libs/agno/agno/knowledge/embedder/vllm.py` | 2
(`async_get_embedding`, `async_get_embedding_and_usage` — local mode
branch) |

## Not changed

- `tracing/exporter.py` — intentionally handles both running and
non-running loop contexts (`loop.is_running()` branch + `asyncio.run()`
fallback), so `get_event_loop()` is appropriate there.
- `knowledge/reader/youtube_reader.py` — already addressed by #8078.

## Testing

- All three files pass `py_compile` syntax check.
- No behavioral change: in an `async def` method, `get_event_loop()` and
`get_running_loop()` return the same loop object. The only difference is
the deprecation warning is eliminated.

fix: memory_topics signature mismatch across DB backends (#7490)

## TL;DR

`GET /memory_topics` has been returning **HTTP 500** on most AgentOS
deployments since **2026-02-11**. This PR fixes the signature mismatch
across **14 sync/async DB backends**, patches a separate **silent tenant
data leak** in MySQL (both sync and async), replaces a **dead
parameter** in Firestore, and adds comprehensive integration tests.

**Security fixes included:**
- RemoteDb now uses `effective_user_id` (JWT-resolved) instead of raw
query param, preventing user_id spoofing attacks
- AgentOSClient methods use keyword-only `user_id` parameter to preserve
backward compatibility

---

## Changes Summary

### 1. Signature Fixes (14 backends)
All `get_all_memory_topics()` implementations now accept `user_id:
Optional[str] = None`:
- PostgresDb, AsyncPostgresDb
- SqliteDb, AsyncSqliteDb  
- MySQLDb, AsyncMySQLDb
- MongoDb, AsyncMongoDb
- DynamoDb, FirestoreDb, GcsJsonDb
- RedisDb, SingleStoreDb, SurrealDb
- InMemoryDb, JsonDb

### 2. Security Fix: RemoteDb User Isolation
**Before (vulnerable):**
```python
return await db.get_memory_topics(
    user_id=user_id,  # Raw query param - attacker can spoof
    ...
)
```

**After (secure):**
```python
return await db.get_memory_topics(
    user_id=effective_user_id,  # JWT-resolved - spoofing blocked
    ...
)
```

The `effective_user_id` comes from `resolve_db_and_scope()` which:
- Returns JWT `sub` when user isolation is ON and caller is a regular
user
- Ignores any `?user_id=attacker` query param manipulation

### 3. Backward Compatibility: AgentOSClient
Added `user_id` as **keyword-only** parameter (after `*,`) to preserve
positional arg compatibility:

```python
# Before: would break client.get_memory_topics("prod-db")
async def get_memory_topics(self, user_id=None, db_id=None, ...)

# After: positional callers still work
async def get_memory_topics(self, db_id=None, table=None, headers=None, *, user_id=None)
```

### 4. Bug Fixes
- **SQLite**: Fixed to iterate ALL rows (was only reading first row's
topics)
- **SQLite**: Added JSON parsing for topic arrays stored as strings
- **SurrealDB**: Added None check in `utils.py` query function
- **Firestore**: Removed spurious `create_collection_if_not_found`
parameter
- **MySQL**: Now actually uses `user_id` in query (was accepting but
ignoring)
- **DynamoDB**: Fixed topics extraction path

### 5. Integration Tests Added
- MongoDB (mongomock): 11 tests
- PostgreSQL (sync): 3 new tests
- PostgreSQL (async): 3 new tests
- SQLite: 4 new tests
- MySQL (async): 3 new tests
- InMemoryDb: 3 new tests

All tests verify:
- `user_id` filtering works correctly
- Unknown user returns empty list
- Tenant isolation (Alice can't see Bob's topics)

---

## The bug in one picture

```
  GET /memory_topics?user_id=alice
              │
              ▼
  ┌─────────────────────────────┐
  │  FastAPI Router              │
  │  async def get_topics(...)   │
  │  user_id = "alice"           │
  │  db = PostgresDb(...)        │
  └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
        db.get_all_memory_topics(user_id=user_id)
                 │
                 ▼
        ┌─────────────────────────────┐
        │ Concrete signature:         │
        │  def get_all_memory_topics  │
        │    (self)  ← missing user_id│
        │                             │
        │ → TypeError: unexpected     │
        │   keyword argument 'user_id'│
        └─────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
        500 Internal Server Error
```

---

## Security Flow (after fix)

```
  GET /memory_topics?user_id=attacker
  Authorization: Bearer <bob_jwt>
              │
              ▼
  resolve_db_and_scope(fallback_user_id="attacker")
              │
              ├── user_isolation = True
              ├── JWT sub = "bob"
              ├── Not admin
              │
              ▼
  effective_user_id = "bob"  ← JWT wins, "attacker" ignored
              │
              ▼
  db.get_all_memory_topics(user_id="bob")
              │
              ▼
  Returns only Bob's topics (attacker blocked)
```

fix: skip strict tool mode when a parser_model is set (#8123)

## Summary

When an agent has both an `output_schema` and a `parser_model`, the base
model's tools were still being forced into strict (structured-outputs)
mode. That's inconsistent with how `parser_model` is treated everywhere
else — and on providers that compile a grammar from strict tool schemas
(Anthropic) it breaks any agent with more than a few tools:

```
400 invalid_request_error: "The compiled grammar is too large, which would cause
performance issues. Simplify your tool schemas or reduce the number of strict tools."
```

Since it's a non-retryable 400 on the base model, the run fails and the
`parser_model` never runs, so no structured output is produced.

**Root cause:** the strict-mode gate in `parse_tools()`
(`libs/agno/agno/agent/_tools.py`) didn't account for `parser_model`.
The whole point of `parser_model` is that the base model does **not**
produce the structured output — a separate, tool-less `parser_model`
call does. Agno already encodes this elsewhere:

- `_run.py` (`run_dispatch` / `arun_dispatch`): `response_format =
get_response_format(...) if agent.parser_model is None else None`
- `_messages.py`: the JSON-output prompt is added only when
`agent.parser_model is None`

`parse_tools()` was the only structured-output gate missing the
`parser_model is None` check, so the base model's tools stayed strict,
which enabled the `structured-outputs-2025-11-13` beta and forced
Anthropic to compile a combined grammar over every tool schema.

**Fix** (one line): add the same `parser_model is None` guard the other
gates use, so the base model's tools are not marked strict when a
`parser_model` will produce the structured output.

```python
strict = False
if (
    output_schema is not None
    and agent.parser_model is None        # base model isn't producing structured output here
    and (agent.structured_outputs or (not agent.use_json_mode))
    and model.supports_native_structured_outputs
):
    strict = True
```

`parse_tools()` is shared by `get_tools()` and `aget_tools()` (via
`determine_tools_for_model`), so this fixes both the sync and async
paths.

( Issue number: #8122 )

fix: add _acontinue_run_background_stream to prevent AttributeError on continue-run SSE (#8136)

## Problem

Calling `team.acontinue_run(background=True, stream=True)` (used by the
AgentOS `/teams/{id}/runs/{id}/continue` endpoint with
`background=True&stream=True`) crashes with:

```
AttributeError: 'RunContinuedEvent' object has no attribute 'encode'
```

The traceback lands in `starlette/responses.py`:
```
chunk = chunk.encode(self.charset)
        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'RunContinuedEvent' object has no attribute 'encode'
```

Fixes #8134

### Root cause

`acontinue_run_dispatch` had no `background` parameter and no
`_acontinue_run_background_stream` function existed. When
`background=True` was passed in `**kwargs`, it silently fell through to
`_acontinue_run_stream`, which yields raw `TeamRunOutputEvent` /
`RunContinuedEvent` objects.

`team_resumable_continue_response_streamer` in the router then `yield
sse_data` those raw objects directly into `StreamingResponse` — which
calls `.encode()` on every chunk and raises the `AttributeError`.

Contrast with the normal `run()` path: `_arun_background_stream` already
exists and yields **pre-formatted SSE strings** (not raw events) so
`.encode()` works fine.

## Fix

1. **Added `_acontinue_run_background_stream`** — mirrors
`_arun_background_stream` but drives `_acontinue_run_stream` internally.
Formats every event with `format_sse_event_with_index` before queuing,
so the router receives plain strings.

2. **Updated `acontinue_run_dispatch`** — pops `background` from
`**kwargs` (preventing it leaking into `_acontinue_run_stream`) and
routes `background=True, stream=True` to
`_acontinue_run_background_stream`.

## Tests

Added `libs/agno/tests/unit/test_acontinue_run_background_stream.py` (3
pure unit tests, no live server required):

| test | what it checks |
|---|---|
| `test_background_kwarg_not_forwarded_to_acontinue_run_stream` |
`_acontinue_run_stream` has no `background` param |
| `test_background_kwarg_is_popped_in_dispatch` |
`acontinue_run_dispatch` accepts `**kwargs` |
| `test_background_stream_yields_strings_not_events` |
`_acontinue_run_background_stream` yields `str`, not raw events |

```
pytest libs/agno/tests/unit/test_acontinue_run_background_stream.py -v
3 passed
```

fix: tools use async entrypoint in async execution chain when no hooks configured (#7765)

Fixes #7716.

When `tool_hooks=[]` (empty list), `_build_nested_execution_chain_async`
returns the sync `execute_entrypoint` instead of the async one. The
check `if self.function.tool_hooks is not None` is `True` for an empty
list, so it enters the hooks branch. Inside, `not
self.function.tool_hooks` is also `True` for an empty list, hitting the
no-hooks fallback which returns the sync entrypoint. Async tool
functions then run synchronously, potentially blocking the event loop.

Changed the fallback to return `execute_entrypoint_async`, which already
handles both sync and async functions correctly via
`iscoroutinefunction`. Added a regression test verifying async tools
with `tool_hooks=[]` execute correctly. All 51 existing tests in
`test_functions.py` pass.

fix: replace blocking `time.sleep` with `await asyncio.sleep` in `_async_create_collection_and_scope` (#8158)

Fixes #8157

## Summary

`CouchbaseSearch._async_create_collection_and_scope` is an `async def`
function, but the post-drop wait was implemented with `time.sleep(1)`,
which blocks the entire asyncio event loop for one second on every
collection overwrite. While the loop is blocked, no other coroutines can
run — tool calls, model streams, callbacks, other vectordb writes, and
the agent loop itself are all frozen for that window.

The fix replaces the blocking call with `await asyncio.sleep(1)`, which
yields control to the event loop and matches the pattern already used by
`_async_wait_for_index_ready` later in the same file.

## Affected location

`libs/agno/agno/vectordb/couchbase/couchbase.py:752` — one line changed
from `time.sleep(1)` to `await asyncio.sleep(1)`.

## Regression test


`tests/unit/vectordb/test_couchbase.py::test_async_create_collection_does_not_block_event_loop`
asserts via `inspect.getsource` that the method does not call
`time.sleep` and does call `asyncio.sleep`, so a future revert would
fail in CI immediately.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Behavior

Functionally equivalent — the wait duration is still 1 second; only the
blocking semantics change.

fix: close audio file handle in `OpenAITools.transcribe_audio` (resource leak) (#8161)

Fixes #8160

## Summary

`OpenAITools.transcribe_audio` was opening the audio file with a bare
`open(audio_path, "rb")` whose result was bound to a local variable and
never explicitly closed. On every call — success OR failure — the file
descriptor leaked. For an agent invoking transcription in a loop (batch
processing, streaming audio chunks), this exhausts the process's
`RLIMIT_NOFILE` and the next `open()` raises `OSError: [Errno 24] Too
many open files`.

The fix wraps the call in a `with open(...) as audio_file:` block so the
file is closed deterministically at the end of the API call regardless
of whether `audio.transcriptions.create(...)` succeeds or raises.

No behavior change in the success or failure paths beyond the close —
the OpenAI SDK reads the file fully during the request, so closing it
right after the response is returned is safe.

## Affected location

`libs/agno/agno/tools/openai.py:90` — inside
`OpenAITools.transcribe_audio`. One change: `audio_file =
open(audio_path, "rb")` → `with open(audio_path, "rb") as audio_file:`
(and indenting the API call into the `with` body).

## Regression test


`tests/unit/tools/test_openai_tools.py::test_transcribe_audio_uses_context_manager_to_close_audio_file`
asserts via `inspect.getsource` that the function body uses `with
open(...)` and does NOT contain the buggy `audio_file = open(...)`
assignment pattern, so a future revert would fail in CI immediately.

fix: use async Attachment.read() instead of blocking requests.get in Discord client (#8186)

## Summary

`DiscordClient`'s async `on_message` handler called the synchronous,
blocking `requests.get()` to download video and document attachments. A
blocking network call inside a coroutine freezes the entire asyncio
event loop for the full duration of the download, stalling every other
message, typing indicator, and concurrent agent run handled by the bot.

media.read()`, which downloads the attachment without blocking the event
loop. It also downloads through the bot's authenticated session,

feat: stream sub-agent events from context providers (#7924)

## Summary

Streams sub-agent events from context providers to the calling agent.
When a parent agent calls `query_<id>()`, the sub-agent's tool calls
stream in real-time instead of waiting for the final answer.

**Before:** Parent calls `query_wiki("architecture?")` → waits → gets
final JSON. No visibility into sub-agent activity.

**After:** Parent sees sub-agent's `list_files`, `read_file` tool calls
streaming in real-time, then gets the final answer.

## Changes

### Base class (`context/provider.py`)

- Add `stream_sub_agent_events: bool = True` parameter (opt-out, not
opt-in)
- Add `_aget_query_agent()` hook for providers to return their sub-agent
- Convert `_query_tool()` to async generator that yields events then
final JSON
- Set `parent_run_id` on events for frontend nesting (preserves existing
if already set)

### Provider implementations

Each provider implements `_aget_query_agent()` to return its sub-agent:

| Provider | Notes |
|----------|-------|
| Wiki | `_ensure_read_agent()` |
| Web | `_ensure_agent()` |
| GDrive | `_ensure_agent()` |
| Filesystem | `_ensure_agent()` |
| Gmail | `_ensure_read_agent()` |
| Calendar | `_ensure_read_agent()` |
| Database | `_ensure_read_agent()` |
| Slack | `_select_read_agent(run_context)` |
| Workspace | `_ensure_agent()` |
| MCP | `await _aensure_agent()` (async session) |

## How it works

```python
# _query_tool is now an async generator
async def _query(question: str, run_context: RunContext | None = None):
    agent = await provider._aget_query_agent(run_context)
    
    # Stream sub-agent events with parent linkage
    async for event in agent.arun(question, stream=True, stream_events=True):
        if isinstance(event, (RunOutput, TeamRunOutput)):
            final_output = event
            continue
        event.parent_run_id = getattr(event, "parent_run_id", None) or run_id
        yield event
    
    # Yield final answer as JSON
    yield json.dumps(answer_from_run(final_output))
```

The model's `arun_function_calls()` already handles async generator
tools — it spawns a background task, drains events through an
`asyncio.Queue`, and yields them upstream.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for streaming flow (`test_provider.py`,
`test_wiki_provider.py`)
- [x] Tested with os.agno.com UI — nested tool calls visible in
real-time
- [x] Backwards compatible — providers without `_aget_query_agent()`
fall back to `aquery()`

feat: add Manifest for per-entity OS UI metadata (#8142)

## Summary

Adds a top-level `manifest` field on `AgentOSConfig` that holds UI-only
metadata for each agent/team/workflow in the OS. Three fields today,
room to grow:

- **`description`** — short blurb shown on the AgentOS home/landing
card. Unrelated to `Agent.description` / `Team.description` /
`Workflow.description`, which are sent to the model.
- **`labels`** — `list[str]` (badges) or `dict[str, str]` (key/value
tags), shown on the home card.
- **`quick_prompts`** — `list[str]` (max 3), shown on the chat page as
starter prompts.

The map is keyed by the agent/team/workflow id, so a single entry
declares everything the OS UI needs for that entity in one place — no
duplication across multiple buckets.

`ChatConfig` is **left untouched**. Existing configs that set
`chat.quick_prompts={id: [...]}` continue to work unchanged.

### Why a single per-id map (and not split per surface)

Earlier exploration (see closed PRs #8108, #8109) tried nesting fields
under `chat` or splitting them across a `home`/`chat` pair of top-level
fields. Both shapes ended up either misleading (mixing surfaces under
one bucket) or redundant (forcing callers to repeat the entity id under
each surface). Keying by id once and grouping all UI metadata for that
id under a single `Manifest` is the simplest shape that doesn't lie
about scope.

The render-surface mapping (which field shows where) lives in the
`Manifest` docstring and the framework/frontend code, not in the schema.

### Schema (`libs/agno/agno/os/config.py`)

```python
class Manifest(BaseModel):
    description: Optional[str] = None
    labels: Optional[Union[List[str], Dict[str, str]]] = None
    quick_prompts: Optional[List[str]] = None  # max 3, enforced

class AgentOSConfig(BaseModel):
    ...
    chat: Optional[ChatConfig] = None        # untouched
    manifest: Optional[Dict[str, Manifest]] = None   # new
    ...
```

### YAML

```yaml
manifest:
  marketing-agent:
    description: "Plans, runs and reports on marketing campaigns."
    labels: ["beta", "marketing"]
    quick_prompts:
      - "What can you do?"
      - "How is our latest post working?"
      - "Tell me about our active marketing campaigns"
  support-team:
    description: "Triages and routes incoming support tickets."
    labels:
      env: "prod"
      team: "growth"
```

### Python

```python
config=AgentOSConfig(
    manifest={
        "marketing-agent": Manifest(
            description="Plans, runs and reports on marketing campaigns.",
            labels=["beta", "marketing"],
            quick_prompts=["What can you do?", "..."],
        ),
    },
)
```

### Cookbook

`cookbook/05_agent_os/os_config/` (`basic.py` and `config.yaml`) is
updated to demo the new shape. Other cookbook configs (`00_quickstart`,
`01_demo`, `levels_of_agentic_software`, `shopify_demo`) are left on the
legacy `chat.quick_prompts` form to exercise backward compatibility
in-tree.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Frontend impact (action required)

This is fully backward compatible at the config-input level. The change
for the frontend is that there's a new source of truth for these fields:

1. Render `manifest[id].description` and `manifest[id].labels` on the
home/landing card.
2. Prefer `manifest[id].quick_prompts` over `chat.quick_prompts[id]`
when both are present (or pick a precedence and document it). Both will
appear in `/config` responses until the legacy field is sunsetted.

No existing fields on the `/config` response are removed by this PR.
`chat.quick_prompts` is unchanged.

feat: agui state events (#6080)

## Summary

Completes the outbound half of AG-UI state synchronization. The AG-UI
interface now emits `StateSnapshotEvent` and `StateDeltaEvent` events
during streaming, enabling frontend clients (e.g. CopilotKit) to receive
real-time state updates from the agent.

Previously, agno accepted state from the frontend (`run_input.state` ->
`agent.arun(session_state=...)`) but never sent updated state back. This
PR closes that loop.

Closes #6136

### What changed

- **`pyproject.toml`**: Added `jsonpatch` to `agui` extras and mypy
overrides
- **`utils.py`**: Extended `EventBuffer` with state tracking
(`set_state_snapshot`, `compute_state_delta`), added
`_create_state_delta_events()` helper, threaded `run_state` through both
streaming functions and event creation
- **`router.py`**: Emit initial `StateSnapshotEvent` after
`RunStartedEvent`, pass `run_state` to streaming functions (both
`run_agent()` and `run_team()`)
- **Tests**: 6 new unit tests + integration test file with mocked and
real API tests

### Event sequence (run with state + tools)

```
RUN_STARTED
STATE_SNAPSHOT          <- initial state
TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END
TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/END
TOOL_CALL_RESULT
STATE_DELTA             <- JSON Patch ops (RFC 6902) if state changed
TEXT_MESSAGE_START/CONTENT/END
STATE_SNAPSHOT          <- final authoritative state
RUN_FINISHED
```

### Design decisions

- **Deep-copy isolation**: `_last_snapshot` stores a deep copy so
in-place mutations to the agent's state dict are detectable via
`jsonpatch.make_patch()`
- **Mutable dict reference chain**: `session_state` (the validated dict)
is passed as `run_state` through the entire pipeline, so tool-induced
mutations are visible at delta computation time
- **Backward compatible**: All state event emission is gated on
`run_state is not None` - when the frontend sends no state, zero state
events are emitted
- **Final snapshot uses authoritative source**: Uses
`RunCompletedEvent.session_state` when available, falls back to
`run_state`

fix: pin ag-ui-protocol>=0.1.14 to prevent reasoning role validation error (#8169)

## Summary

Pins `ag-ui-protocol>=0.1.14` in `libs/agno/pyproject.toml` to prevent
the Pydantic validation error from issue #7556 at install time.

## Root cause

Versions `<= 0.1.13` of `ag-ui-protocol` defined
`ReasoningMessageStartEvent.role` as `Literal["assistant"]`. agno emits
`role="reasoning"` (correctly aligned with the TypeScript SDK), which
fails Pydantic validation on those older versions and crashes the AGUI
stream mid-run.

Version `0.1.14` (released 2026-03-18, ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui#1200)
changed the literal to `Literal["reasoning"]`, aligning the Python SDK
with the TypeScript SDK and with what agno emits.

## Fix

`libs/agno/pyproject.toml:200`:

```diff
-agui = ["ag-ui-protocol"]
+agui = ["ag-ui-protocol>=0.1.14"]
```

This is the cleaner alternative to the runtime-introspection approach
proposed in #7573 (closed). Pinning the dep makes the bug unreachable at
install time rather than masking it at runtime.

## Verification

- Constraint syntax validated via `packaging.requirements.Requirement`
(PEP 440)
- `>=0.1.14` excludes 0.1.13 (buggy) and includes 0.1.14, 0.1.15,
0.1.16, 0.1.18 (fixed)
- Currently installed `0.1.18` satisfies the constraint, so dev
environments are not affected
- 0.1.14 was verified as the first PyPI release containing PR #1200 by
inspecting wheel contents of 0.1.13 (still `Literal["assistant"]`) vs
0.1.14 (now `Literal["reasoning"]`)

fix: enable_agentic_state tool receives correct schema for dict params (#8231)

## Summary
- Fixes bare `dict` type hint generating `additionalProperties: false`
in JSON schema
- This caused `update_session_state` tool to receive empty `{}` from LLM
in infinite loops

## Root Cause
When `enable_agentic_state=True`, the `update_session_state` tool's
`session_state_updates: dict` parameter was being converted to a JSON
schema with `additionalProperties: false`. This told the LLM "no keys
are allowed", causing it to call the tool with `{}` repeatedly.

The fix adds explicit handling for bare `dict` type hint in
`get_json_schema_for_arg()`:
```python
if type_hint is dict:
    return {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": True}
```

Also improved `Dict[K, V]` handling to properly use `propertyNames` and
typed `additionalProperties`.

fix: guard against IndexError when runs list is empty in from_dict (#8187)

## Bug

`AgentSession.from_dict` and `TeamSession.from_dict` access `runs[0]`
before checking whether the list is non-empty:

```python
# Both files, same line:
if runs is not None and isinstance(runs[0], dict):
```

When `runs` is an empty list `[]`, the short-circuit evaluation stops at
`runs is not None` (True) and then immediately evaluates `runs[0]`,
raising:

```
IndexError: list index out of range
```

**Trigger**: This happens whenever a session is round-tripped through
`to_dict()`/`from_dict()` with no runs yet recorded — a valid state for
a freshly created session.

```python
session = AgentSession(session_id="x", runs=[])
AgentSession.from_dict(session.to_dict())  # <- IndexError
```

## Fix

Replace the two-part guard with a single truthiness check, which
correctly handles `None`, `[]`, and non-empty lists in one expression:

```python
# Before
if runs is not None and isinstance(runs[0], dict):

# After  
if runs and isinstance(runs[0], dict):
```

Both `AgentSession` (`session/agent.py`) and `TeamSession`
(`session/team.py`) had the same pattern and are fixed together.

fix: close text message before reasoning events in AG-UI (#5466) (#8251)

## Summary

Fixes #5466 - AG-UI with reasoning tools throws event ordering errors.

The bug: When an agent with ReasoningTools (or native reasoning models
like o4-mini) streams text and then reasoning events, the AG-UI protocol
was violated:

```
Event sequence: TEXT_MESSAGE_START → TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT → REASONING_START → ...
                                                            ↑ VIOLATION!
```

The AG-UI protocol requires `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` before starting a new
message type. Clients (like CopilotKit) enforce this and throw:
> "Cannot send event type 'X' after 'TEXT_MESSAGE_START': Send
'TEXT_MESSAGE_END' first."

**Root cause:** The reasoning event handlers in
`_create_events_from_chunk()` didn't close open text messages before
emitting reasoning events, unlike the tool call handlers which already
did this correctly.

## Changes

- Added text message closing logic to all 3 reasoning event handlers:
  - `ReasoningStartedEvent` 
  - `ReasoningContentDeltaEvent` (native model reasoning)
  - `ReasoningStepEvent` (ReasoningTools think/analyze)
- Added 3 regression tests that reproduce the exact protocol violation

## Summary

This targets the single `MCPTools` path discussed in #8156, where
`refresh_connection=True` plus dynamic HTTP headers can leave a per-run
streamable-http session to be cleaned up later from a different task.
The MCP HTTP client keeps anyio cancel scopes inside its async context
managers, so that delayed cross-task cleanup can surface as `Attempted

- open, initialize, use, and close that temporary HTTP session inside
the same tool-call task
- keep the existing cached per-run session behavior for the normal
`refresh_connection=False` path and for `MultiMCPTools`

populate `_run_sessions` / `_run_session_contexts` and close both

fix: json_schema handle Optional dataclass fields without a type (#8329)

## What's broken

Registering a tool whose parameter is a dataclass with a field like
`Optional[Literal[1, "a"]]` crashes schema generation.
`get_json_schema_for_arg` does `schema["type"]` on every `anyOf` member,
but some members legitimately have no `type` — a mixed-type `Literal`
renders as `{"enum": [...]}` — so it raises `KeyError: 'type'`. The
public caller wraps this in `try/except`, so the result is worse than a
crash: the entire parameter is silently dropped and the model never
learns the argument exists.

```python
@dataclass
class Config:
    mode: Optional[Literal[1, "a"]] = None

get_json_schema_for_arg(Config)   # -> KeyError: 'type'
```

## Why it happens

`schema["type"]` is dereferenced unconditionally over `anyOf` members,
which aren't guaranteed to carry a `type` key.

## Fix

Use `schema.get("type")` and only collapse `anyOf` to a single `type`
when a concrete non-null type exists; otherwise leave `anyOf` intact
(still valid JSON Schema).

## Test

A dataclass with `Optional[Literal[1, "a"]]` now produces a schema
instead of raising.

Fixes #8328

feat: auto-populate AgentOS registry from agents, teams, and workflows (#8269)

## Summary

AgentOS now auto-populates its `Registry` with the components found
inside its agents, teams, and workflows. On construction it recursively
walks every agent, team, and workflow and collects the **models**,
**tools**, **databases**, and **vector databases** they reference, so
`GET /registry` reflects what is actually wired into the OS without
requiring those components to be declared a second time.

Previously the registry auto-discovered agents, teams, knowledge, and
managers, but models/tools/dbs/vector_dbs were only populated if
hand-passed to `Registry(...)`. This closes that gap.

**Behavior**
- Default-on, no flag (consistent with the existing
`_populate_registry_*` methods, which are all unconditional).
- The walk covers nested teams and every workflow step type: `Steps`,
`Loop`, `Parallel`, `Condition` (including `else_steps`), `Router`
(including `choices`), and nested workflows.
- Models collected include `reasoning_model`, `parser_model`,
`output_model`, and fallback models (both raw `fallback_models` and the
post-init `fallback_config`). Vector dbs and contents dbs are pulled
from knowledge.
- Deduplication by id/name: a model shared across many agents is
collected once, and components passed to a `Registry` explicitly are
preserved (discovered ones are merged in, never duplicated).
- User objects are only referenced, never mutated. Remote/factory and
callable components are skipped. Per-node guards keep a malformed node
from failing AgentOS construction.
- Wired into all three population sites (`__init__`, `resync`,
`get_app`); idempotent.

No API or schema changes: the existing `GET /registry` router already
serializes models/tools/dbs/vector_dbs, so it simply returns more rows.

feat: CRUD endpoints for learnings on AgentOS (#7826)

## Summary

Adds `/learnings` REST endpoints to AgentOS for CRUD over the existing
`agno_learnings` table — the table that backs the learning stores
(`user_profile`, `user_memory`, `entity_memory`, `session_context`,
`decision_log`) — plus the supporting DB-layer methods, RBAC, config
plumbing, and a cookbook.

> Originally just the five CRUD verbs; the branch has since grown (via
#8299/#8301/#8303/#8366/#8367/#8368 and follow-ups) into the full
surface below. Updating this description to match.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/learnings` | Paginated list. Filters: `learning_type`,
`user_id`, `agent_id`, `team_id`, `session_id`, `namespace`,
`entity_id`, `entity_type`. Sorting: `sort_by` + `sort_order`. |
| `POST` | `/learnings` | Create. Id is derived **deterministically**
for identity-keyed types (see below); generated uuid otherwise. |
| `GET` | `/learnings/users` | Lightweight index of the users that own
learnings (`user_id` + `last_learning_updated_at`), with
`sort_by`/`sort_order`. |
| `DELETE` | `/learnings/users/{user_id}` | Delete all of a user's
learnings (optionally one `learning_type`). |
| `GET` | `/learnings/{learning_id}` | Fetch a single record. |
| `PATCH` | `/learnings/{learning_id}` | Replace `content` and/or
`metadata`; identity fields immutable. |
| `DELETE` | `/learnings/{learning_id}` | Delete a record. |

All read/list endpoints also accept `?db_id=` and `?table=` to target a
specific db/table (`table` requires `db_id`).

## POST id derivation (reconciliation)

The stores key records by a deterministic id derived from the identity
fields, not a uuid (`user_profile_{user_id}`, `memories_{user_id}`,
`session_context_{session_id}`,
`entity_{namespace}_{entity_type}_{entity_id}`). `POST` computes the
**same** id (via the new `build_learning_id`, which the stores'
`_build_*_id` helpers now delegate to) so an API-created record
reconciles with what the agent reads/writes — no orphan, no duplicate.
Missing the required identity field → `422`; an existing identity record
→ `409` (use `PATCH`). Other types (e.g. `decision_log`) get a generated
id.

## Auth / RBAC / IDOR

- **User isolation (opt-in).** Scoping uses the framework's
`get_scoped_user_id` (`AuthorizationConfig(user_isolation=True)`).
Admins and isolation-off/no-JWT callers are unscoped (full access). A
scoped non-admin caller is bound to its own `user_id` on
list/create/users/delete-user (mismatch → `403`), and on single-record
fetch cross-user → `404` (no existence leak).
- **Shared (null-owner) records.** `user_id IS NULL` records (global,
agent, team, session, entity learnings) remain **readable** by any
caller, but **mutating** them (PATCH/DELETE) is **admin-only** (`403`
for a regular user).
- **RBAC scope map.** `/learnings` routes are registered in
`get_default_scope_mappings()` with `learnings:read` / `learnings:write`
/ `learnings:delete`, so they aren't open to any authenticated token
when RBAC is enabled.

## DB layer

- `BaseDb` / `AsyncBaseDb`: new non-abstract methods (so third-party
adapters don't break): `get_learning_by_id`, `list_learnings`
(paginated, `(records, total)`), `get_learnings_user_stats`,
`delete_user_learnings`.
- **Full implementations:** postgres, async_postgres, sqlite,
async_sqlite, async_mongo. **Stubs** (matching the per-adapter
`NotImplementedError` style): mongo, redis, in_memory, json; everything
else inherits the `BaseDb` default → router returns `501`.
- **Error convention:** the router-facing methods `log_error` + raise on
failure (router → `500`), so a failed read/list/bulk-delete is surfaced
(no false `204` on the destructive path); the agent-facing
`get_learnings`/`get_learning` keep swallowing per the learn module's
"never crash the agent" rule. Normal empty results are unchanged.
- **Fix:** `async_mongo._get_collection` no longer caches a missing
collection as `None` (a read-before-first-write previously dropped later
writes silently).

## Learning store changes

- Per-entry `created_at`/`updated_at` are now stamped (framework-owned)
on individual user memories and entity facts/events/relationships.
- Dropped the always-null internal/duplicate fields from persisted
`UserProfile` content (they mirror the row columns).

## Config / discovery

- `LearningDomainConfig`/`LearningConfig` wired into `AgentOSConfig` +
`ConfigResponse`; `AgentOS._get_learning_config()`;
`learnings_table_name` added to `_get_db_table_names()` and to
`RemoteDb.from_config()`; `learning` surfaced in both the HTTP `/config`
and the MCP `get_agentos_config` responses.

**Intentionally not exposed:** `workflow_id` (no learning store writes
it) and `learned_knowledge` (stored in the knowledge/vector store, not
`agno_learnings` — served by `/knowledge`).

## Tests & cookbook

- Unit: `test_learnings_router.py`, `test_build_learning_id.py`,
`test_memories_schema.py`, `test_scopes.py` (RBAC),
`test_async_mongo.py` (caching regression), `test_remote_db.py`;
integration `/config`; MCP route test. Covers all verbs, validation,
pagination, sorting, `?table=`, the full IDOR/admin matrix,
deterministic-id/409/422, and DB-error→500.
- Cookbook `cookbook/05_agent_os/learnings/` — server example + httpx
client exercising the full cycle, verified end-to-end against a live
AgentOS.

fix: remove per-response Gemini cleanup causing thread-safety race (#7797)

## Summary

Fixes #7427 — Gemini client thread-safety bug causing SSL/TLS failures
under concurrent load.

- Removes 4 per-response cleanup blocks in `base.py` that were closing
and nulling `self.client` after each Gemini response
- Refactors away the dead `try/finally` blocks that remained after
cleanup removal
- Adds 5 unit tests + 20 integration tests verifying client reuse and
thread-safety
- No behavior change for other model providers

## Root Cause

The cleanup blocks were added in PR #5454 (Nov 2025) for Gemini 3.0
thought signatures. While well-intentioned, closing the client after
each response is the wrong lifecycle scope — it causes race conditions
when multiple concurrent requests share a Gemini model instance:

```
Thread A                           Thread B
├─ get_client() → Creates Client   │
├─ API call (in-flight)            ├─ get_client() → Returns SAME Client
│                                  ├─ API call starts
├─ Response arrives                │  (still in-flight)
├─ CLEANUP: self.client = None  ←──│── BUG: nulls shared client
│                                  ├─ SSL/TLS ERROR (client gone)
```

## Why This Fix Is Safe

### SDK Analysis (google-genai v2.5.0)

The `google-genai` SDK handles lifecycle correctly:

1. **`__del__` handles cleanup automatically** — Both `Client.__del__`
and `BaseApiClient.__del__` call `close()` when garbage collected. No
manual cleanup needed.

2. **Thread-safe design** — SDK uses `threading.Lock` for sync auth and
`asyncio.Lock` (with double-checked locking) for async auth.

3. **httpx is thread-safe** — The SDK uses httpx internally, which is
[documented as thread-safe](https://www.python-httpx.org/api/).

4. **Combined sync/async client** — One `genai.Client` serves both
`.models.*` (sync) and `.aio.models.*` (async) paths. Per-response
cleanup was especially destructive because it killed the shared client
mid-flight.

### Framework Comparison

| Framework | Init | Cleanup | Per-Response Close |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------------|
| **LangChain** | Eager | `__del__` with sync+async close | NO |
| **LlamaIndex** | Eager | None (trusts SDK) | NO |
| **OpenAI SDK** | Eager | `__del__` on httpx wrapper | NO |
| **Agno (fixed)** | Lazy | SDK's `__del__` | NO |
| **Agno (broken)** | Lazy | Per-response close | YES ← BUG |

**No major framework does per-response cleanup** — this was uniquely
wrong in Agno.

## Test Results

| Test Suite | Result |
|------------|--------|
| Unit: `test_gemini_thread_safety.py` | **5/5 PASS** |
| Unit: `test_gemini.py` | **48/48 PASS** |
| Integration: `test_gemini_concurrent_integration.py` | **20/20 PASS**
|
| Manual: 32 concurrent requests, 8 workers | **32/32 PASS, 0 SSL
errors** |

- `test_client_shared_across_threads` — verifies no per-thread
recreation
- `test_user_injected_client_is_preserved` — verifies `client=` param

- `test_user_injected_client_shared_across_threads` — user client not

  - `test_client_persists_after_get_client` — no cleanup after creation

## Deep Verification Round 2 (2026-06-10)

Rebased on `main` and re-verified end to end before force-push.

### SDK lifecycle audit (google-genai 2.8.0, installed source)

- `Client.__del__` / `BaseApiClient.__del__` close transports on GC
(`client.py:685`, `_api_client.py:2183`) — no manual per-response
cleanup needed.
- Auth is lock-protected: `threading.Lock` (sync) + double-checked
`asyncio.Lock` (async) (`_api_client.py:685`, `1170-1193`).
- Vertex/ADC tokens are refreshed automatically per request when expired
(`_api_client.py:2202-2231`) — long-lived clients never hold stale
credentials.
- Cross-event-loop safety: the default async path uses aiohttp, and
`_get_aiohttp_session()` recreates the session when its event loop is
closed (`_api_client.py:921`). Verified live with two sequential
`asyncio.run()` calls on one model.

### Expanded integration coverage (10 new tests, all live)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Client reuse across two event loops (sync + streaming) | PASS |
| Concurrent tool-calling (multi-invocation runs on one client) | PASS |
| Async streaming with tool-call continuation | PASS |
| Interrupted stream then client reuse | PASS |
| Failed request (404) then recovery on same client | PASS |
| Sustained sequential runs, single client identity | PASS |
| Concurrent structured output | PASS |
| deepcopy gets independent client, original untouched | PASS |
| Gemini 3 thought-signature tool round-trip on cached client | PASS |

Full file: **19/19 pass**. Also fixed the two original streaming tests,
which were vacuous: they called `.content` on a generator / `await`ed an
async generator, the `TypeError` was swallowed by the blanket `except`,
and the tests asserted only `ssl_errors == 0`. They now drain streams
and assert success counts.

### Stress soak (issue #5326 pattern)

Team (3 Gemini models) + Postgres + async streaming, progressive load 10
-> 50 concurrent: **150/150 success, 0 timeouts, 0 errors**, first-chunk
latency flat (~1s) at 50 concurrent.

### Adversarial review (independent)

No blocking regression found vs either era (per-response-cleanup era, or
the pre-Nov-2025 cached-client era this PR restores). Known non-blocking
caveats, all pre-existing in kind:

- A used model holds a live client and is no longer picklable
(`_thread.lock`). Identical to every other provider (`OpenAIChat` fails
the same way); agno never pickles models internally; `deepcopy` paths
are unaffected (`Gemini.__deepcopy__` skips the client).
- Fork-after-first-use shares the client with children — the universal
cached-SDK caveat, not Gemini-specific.
- genai's transport retry predicate doesn't cover
`httpx.ReadError`/`RemoteProtocolError` on idle-close races; window is
tiny (httpcore drops dead connections pre-reuse, aiohttp path has an
internal retry) and users can opt into SDK `HttpRetryOptions` via
`client_params` or agno's `Model.retries`.
- `get_client()` first-call check-then-create race can build N clients
under cold concurrent start; extras are GC'd harmlessly. Pre-existing
and benign — see the creation-lock investigation below.

### get_client() creation-lock investigation (2026-06-10) — rejected
with data

Considered adding a creation lock for the first-call `get_client()`
race. Empirical probes against the live API (16 barrier-synchronized
threads; constructor artificially slowed 150ms; 30 concurrent async
users; 4 concurrent event loops sharing one agent) showed:

- The race produces only throwaway clients that are GC-closed after
their request completes — **0 user-visible failures in every topology**,
even engineered worst-case.
- On a single event loop (AgentOS shape) the race is structurally
impossible: `get_client()` has no `await`, so 30 concurrent users
construct exactly 1 client.
- A/B with the lock monkeypatched in: identical results in every
scenario (multi-loop: 18 failures locked vs 18 unlocked). The lock fixes
nothing real.

Not added — consistent with this PR's thesis that client lifecycle
belongs to the SDK.

### Known SDK limitation (pre-existing, improved by this PR)

Sharing one model instance across multiple **concurrently running**
event loops degrades on the async path: the SDK stores a single aiohttp
session per client and aiohttp sessions are loop-bound, so only the
session-owner loop's requests succeed. Measured: `origin/main` fails
**0/24** on this topology (per-response close also killed in-flight
cross-loop requests); this PR improves it to **6/24**. Sequential loops
(`asyncio.run()` twice) are fully supported — the SDK recreates the
session when its loop is closed. Guidance: use one event loop per model
instance for concurrent async work.

### Original issue reproduced and verified fixed (2026-06-10)

Ran #7427's exact recipe (one model instance, ThreadPoolExecutor 16
workers, 4 rounds each, live API) against both trees:

| | main (cleanup present) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Success | 44/64 (**31% failure**) | **64/64** |
| Errors | `Server disconnected without sending a response`, `'NoneType'
object has no attribute 'models'` | none |
| Wall time | 16.7s | 11.6s |

The `NoneType` error is the cleanup race in its purest form (client
nulled between check and use); the server-disconnect errors are the same
mid-flight pool teardown that surfaces as `[SSL:
DECRYPTION_FAILED_OR_BAD_RECORD_MAC]` / `[SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER]` on
Linux under load (fd recycling mid-TLS-record). The 31% failure rate on
main also matches the "50+ concurrent = 30% fail" reported in #5326.

feat: custom, scoped, identity-aware tools for the AgentOS MCP server (+ bug fixes) (#8404)

## Summary

Makes the AgentOS MCP server (served at `/mcp`) a real extension point —
custom tools, scoping, caller-identity injection, per-call gating, and
built-in DNS-rebinding protection — and folds in two independent bug
fixes. Dogfooded against a real product (**@context**), whose
hand-rolled ~200-line owner-only MCP server collapses to a few lines of
config — with **no custom middleware classes** — once AgentOS owns these
concerns.

### What you can do now

```python
from agno.os import AgentOS
from agno.os.config import MCPServerConfig

agent_os = AgentOS(
    agents=[my_agent],
    authorization=True, authorization_config=auth_config,
    enable_mcp_server=True,
    mcp_config=MCPServerConfig(
        tools=[use_context],          # custom tools (plain callables or Agno @tool / Function)
        enable_builtin_tools=False,   # ship ONLY your tools (or scope with include_tags / exclude_tags)
        authorize=is_owner,           # fn(user_id)->bool; 401s before any tool/model runs
        allowed_hosts=["my-app.com"], # built-in DNS-rebinding protection (localhost is automatic)
    ),
)

# A custom tool reads almost like a built-in: declare `user_id` and AgentOS injects the
# authenticated caller (JWT subject) and HIDES it from the client schema (no spoofing).
async def use_context(message: str, session_id: str | None = None, user_id: str | None = None) -> str:
    return (await my_agent.arun(message, user_id=user_id, session_id=session_id)).content
```

**Capabilities**
- **Custom tools** — plain callables and Agno `@tool`/`Function`s; share
the same `/mcp` mount, lifespan, and JWT middleware as the built-ins.
- **Scope the built-ins** — `enable_builtin_tools=False` ships only your
tools; `include_tags`/`exclude_tags` filter by the existing
`core`/`session`/`memory` tags.
- **Identity injection** — a custom tool that declares `user_id` gets
the JWT subject, excluded from the client-facing schema. Power users can
declare a FastMCP `Context` instead.
- **`authorize`** — per-call gate, runs after JWT, 401s before the model
runs.
- **`allowed_hosts` / `allowed_origins`** — built-in DNS-rebinding
protection (Host + Origin validation, localhost baked in). Configured
with **data, not a middleware class**.
- **`middleware`** — escape hatch for arbitrary Starlette middleware.

The design principle the maintainer asked for: if every always-on local
MCP server needs DNS-rebinding protection, AgentOS should provide it —
users opt in with a host list, not by writing an ASGI middleware. The
`middleware=[...]` hook remains for anything bespoke.

### Bug fixes (independent, separately reviewable commits)

- **MCP identity threading** — `run_agent`/`run_team`/`run_workflow`
called `arun(message)` with no identity, so an authenticated caller ran
as anonymous. They now resolve `user_id` (JWT subject) and thread
`user_id` + `session_id` into `arun`.
- **Call-site dependencies merge** — call-site `dependencies` passed to
`agent.run()`/`team.run()` *replaced* the configured
`Agent.dependencies`/`Team.dependencies` wholesale. Because the
Slack/WhatsApp interfaces always pass a non-None call-site
`dependencies` (channel/thread ids), any agent using `dependencies` for
prompt templating (e.g. `instructions="You are {owner_name}'s
assistant"`) lost those vars over those interfaces. Now merges
(`{**configured, **call_site}`, call-site wins on conflict), matching
how `metadata`/`knowledge_filters` already merge. *Behavior change:*
callers that relied on full replacement now keep configured keys
(call-site still wins on conflicts).

### API choice (for review)

- **One `mcp_config=MCPServerConfig(...)` object**, mirroring the
existing `authorization` / `authorization_config` pairing;
`enable_mcp_server=True` keeps working unchanged.
- **Rejected a loose `mcp_tools=[...]` kwarg** — `AgentOS.mcp_tools`
already exists and means *the MCP **client** tools collected from
agents/teams/workflows*; that kwarg would collide. The config object
also groups tools + scoping + gating + transport security cohesively.
- **Registration is the list param** (`mcp_config.tools`), not a
decorator — kept deliberately small.
- **Scoping** is done at registration time (a thin decorator wrapper
over the built-ins), so it does not depend on FastMCP's deprecated
tool-removal API.
- **`authorize` vs `middleware`**: `authorize` is the one-line identity
gate (the common case, no class); `middleware` is the escape hatch for
ASGI-level needs. They don't overlap.

The whole public surface lives in one small config object, so it's easy
to reshape before landing.

### @context as the proof — now zero custom middleware

`context/app/mcp.py` (~200 lines) + ~20 lines of mount/lifespan glue in
`main.py` reduces to one `MCPServerConfig(tools=[use_context],
enable_builtin_tools=False, authorize=is_owner,
allowed_hosts=[deploy_host])`, with the tool declaring `user_id`.
**Deleted entirely:** the second `FastMCP`, `_resolve_caller_id` (→
injected `user_id`), `OwnerOnlyMiddleware` (→ `authorize`), the
transport-security helper + `TransportSecuritySettings` (→
`allowed_hosts`), the JWT re-attach, and the manual mount +
FastMCP-lifespan splice. No hand-written middleware classes remain.

### Backward compatibility

Fully backward compatible. With no `mcp_config`, all 19 built-in tools
are registered and no gate/middleware/host-validation is added —
identical to today. `get_mcp_server()` is split into
`build_mcp_server()` (FastMCP tool surface) + `get_mcp_server()` (HTTP
transport + JWT/authorize/middleware/transport-security) so the tools
can be driven by an in-memory MCP client in tests.
